subject.title: Repeated tool-loop context overflows cause successive auto-compactions after successful compaction (v2026.5.5)

question: Which terminal recovery policy should OpenClaw guarantee when compaction succeeds but the rebuilt prompt remains over the effective budget?
rationale: The reports show multiple valid causes and competing remedies—projected tool-result truncation, an immediate stronger reduction, a bounded second compaction, or a successor-session path—whose data-loss, latency, and session-continuity tradeoffs require maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt a post-compaction fit invariant
options.body: Require recovery to re-measure the rebuilt provider-boundary prompt and use a bounded stronger reduction or successor path when it still does not fit.

options.title: Retain current bounded-blocked behavior
options.body: Keep the current retry budget and explicit blocked response, treating manual reset or a new session as the intended terminal recovery path.

options.title: Split by trigger only
options.body: Land narrow fixes for aggregate pressure and estimator inflation without defining a shared successful-but-insufficient recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt a post-compaction fit invariant
recommendation.body: Require recovery to re-measure the rebuilt provider-boundary prompt and use a bounded stronger reduction or successor path when it still does not fit.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner merged the current aggregate-pressure recovery policy and is best positioned to route the policy decision with adjacent embedded-runner contributors.
